title: Island ledgers: First qualifying slip
summary: links is a symmetric 0/1 adjacency matrix. Start a depth-first traversal at each still-unvisited vertex, in increasing index order. Produce the number of vertices in each component, in that start order. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.
descriptionMd:
An inspector follows each cable family fully before starting another unvisited switchboard island. Mina needs the first qualifying slip while the courier waits at the door. Later matches must not jump ahead in the tray.

links is a symmetric 0/1 adjacency matrix. Start a depth-first traversal at each still-unvisited vertex, in increasing index order. Produce the number of vertices in each component, in that start order.

Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.

Implement islandLedgersFirstQualifyingSlip(links, k). Use k exactly where specified above.
unitIntro: Graph depth-first components. links is a symmetric 0/1 adjacency matrix. Start a depth-first traversal at each still-unvisited vertex, in increasing index order. Produce the number of vertices in each component, in that start order. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.
The adjacency matrix is square and has at most 16 vertices; binary entries are 0 or 1, weighted entries are 0 through 13.

Target time O(V^2); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with graph depth-first components. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

links is a symmetric 0/1 adjacency matrix. Start a depth-first traversal at each still-unvisited vertex, in increasing index order. Produce the number of vertices in each component, in that start order. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.
